Chapter Nine: Wrestling with Doubt and Faith in the Present.
You know, for a lot of us today, the story of Jesus is both something we’ve heard a thousand times—and yet, it still feels a little mysterious. The words from the gospels echo in churches and pop up in everyday conversations, but the world they describe can seem so far away. And those big questions that the very first followers of Jesus faced—like, who was he really? What did he mean? And how do you actually live out his teachings?—well, those questions are still hanging around.
Picture this: someone sitting alone, Bible open, just wrestling with doubt. Maybe the stories are beautiful, but then they stumble over some contradictions. The miracles sound impossible. Sometimes, the teachings are just plain hard to understand. And yet—there’s something in that story that keeps pulling at them. Maybe it’s a sense of hope. Maybe it’s the longing for something more. Or maybe, it’s just the simple desire to believe.
Most folks don’t talk much about their doubts. There’s this worry that if you start questioning the story of Jesus, you’ll lose your faith, or maybe even disappoint the people around you. But here’s something to pay attention to: the history of Christianity is packed with people who weren’t afraid to ask tough questions. People who struggled with uncertainty, and, through that struggle, found new ways to believe.
It turns out, faith isn’t about never doubting. It’s about being willing to keep searching, even when you don’t have all the answers. The story of Jesus actually invites us to bring our questions, to be real about the things we struggle with, and to look for meaning—even when everything feels uncertain. For a lot of people, that’s when faith really starts to feel alive. Not because of easy answers, but because of the courage to keep asking.
The journey of faith? It’s never a straight line. There are twists and turns, moments when things suddenly make sense, and other times when everything feels confusing. But the story of Jesus—with all its complexity and contradictions—gives us a way to walk this path. Not by handing us every answer, but by inviting us to keep going, with honesty and hope.
